stem:
Simon is an 8-week-old infant with fever (38.9°C), fussiness and poor feeding. He is unsettled but clinically well perfused, with no focal findings on examination.

Which ONE of the following investigation plans is the most appropriate?

options.text: FBC, blood culture, CXR, LP, urine MC&S

explanation: In a febrile infant under 3 months, a full sepsis work-up is generally indicated, including blood tests, blood culture, urine testing, chest radiograph if clinically indicated, and lumbar puncture in the youngest infants or where serious bacterial infection cannot be excluded. Among the options given, the most appropriate and comprehensive investigation set is option E.
rationale: The source item appears to be asking which investigation set is most appropriate for a young febrile infant. Of the existing options, E is the only one that reflects a broad sepsis evaluation in an infant under 3 months.

optionExplanations.A: A febrile 8-week-old requires investigation for serious bacterial infection; no investigations would be inappropriate.
optionExplanations.B: This is incomplete for a febrile infant of this age because it omits other key sepsis investigations.
optionExplanations.C: Urinalysis alone is insufficient in a young febrile infant.
optionExplanations.D: Useful blood tests, but incomplete without urine studies and further sepsis evaluation.
optionExplanations.E: This is the most comprehensive option and best matches a full febrile infant work-up.

Instructions

There are 3 questions that relate to this scenario.

Clinical scenario 1 - Simon

Simon, an eight week old infant, presents with fussiness and poor feeding for two days. Simon’s older siblings have had an URTI recently and have been exposed to him. On examination he handled well but mostly is unsettled and grizzly.

RR 30/min

HR 160/min

temperature 38.9°C

The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

The following three questions refer to Simon’s clinical scenario.
